official_measurement_examples.name: Part 16 planning route
official_measurement_examples.fact: Electronic communications code operators can use Part 16 permitted-development rights in specified circumstances, but the right is subject to statutory limitations, conditions and in some cases prior approval or notification.

official_measurement_examples.name: Code rights separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Electronic Communications Code regulates legal relationships and rights between site providers and Code operators; Code rights do not by themselves grant planning permission for every apparatus installation.

official_measurement_examples.name: Prior approval distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Some Part 16 development requires local planning authority prior approval on defined matters; prior approval is not the same procedural route as a full planning application and does not erase other statutory requirements.

official_measurement_examples.name: Sensitive locations
official_measurement_examples.fact: Electronic communications permitted-development rights can be more restricted in sensitive locations and designated land; generic Part 16 eligibility must not be assumed without location-specific checks.

official_measurement_examples.name: ICNIRP evidence scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: NPPF requires specified ICNIRP-related self-certification evidence for relevant mast/base-station applications; that certificate does not establish land rights, title or general planning acceptability.

official_measurement_examples.name: Code operator status
official_measurement_examples.fact: Code operator status is granted through the communications regulatory framework and is distinct from ownership of a proposed site or an individual planning consent.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 reform evidence
official_measurement_examples.fact: The current reform call for evidence discusses possible future changes to telecoms planning rules; proposals under review must not be treated as already enacted Part 16 rights.

official_measurement_examples.name: Parcel limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Telecommunications policy, Code rights or a prior-approval route do not establish parcel ownership, unrestricted access rights, exact buildable area or final development yield.

core_rules: Code rights are not planning permission
Part16 is not unlimited development right
prior approval is not full planning permission
operator status is not land ownership
ICNIRP self-certification is not land-right evidence
reform call for evidence is not enacted law
planning permission does not itself create Code rights
Code rights do not establish development yield
network need does not establish site access
fee category does not prove permission route
no parcel telecom clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
